stem: The table shows the design of six studies, each of which compared two treatments using participants from a population P. For how many of the six studies can a cause-and-effect conclusion about the treatments be generalized to all of population P?

figure.title: Design of six studies
columns: Participants selected at random from P

solution: A cause-and-effect conclusion needs random assignment of the treatments.
Generalizing to all of P needs participants selected at random from P.
Only studies 2 and 5 have both, so the answer is 2.
verify:
n = sum(1 for r in figure['rows'] if r[1] == 'Yes' and r[2] == 'Yes')
assert n == 2
assert [Rational(a) for a in spr_answers] == [n]
